Advanced Energy Materials | 🔬 Research Article
💡 Machine learning screened pore-structure windows from a large dataset, guiding synthesis of three model carbon hosts. The work reveals how pore structure governs sulfur speciation and CEI spatial-composition, dictating competition between polysulfide reactions and solvent decomposition. This data-driven strategy links physical host metrics to complex reaction mechanisms, enabling balanced carbon cathodes with 1249.4 mAh g⁻¹ initial capacity and 784.8 mAh g⁻¹ retention after 500 cycles.

💡 The novelty lies in using overpotential decoupling and molecular dynamics to show acetonitrile co-solvent improves fast-charge acceptance by reducing concentration gradients via lower viscosity and enhanced Li+ solvation-shell lability. Significance: identifies transport limitations as the primary barrier, demonstrates electrolyte engineering with interface-stabilizing additives, and reveals NMC811 electrode architecture/loading dominates overpotential, guiding electrode design for extreme fast charging.

Advanced Materials | 🔬 Research Article
💡 The novelty lies in using Bi-mediated Zn extraction to create carbon defects adjacent to Fe-N4 sites, tuning the local microenvironment. This lowers the Fe d-band center, weakens excessive *OH binding, and shifts the potential-limiting step, boosting ORR activity (0.918 V half-wave) and durability (3000 h at −40°C in Zn-air battery). It offers a neighboring-template route for designing efficient single-atom catalysts.
